[b]"The Master should be the most Humble Servant"[/b]
[i][sub]~ Overseer Superior Li Jinping[/sub][/i]

Technocratic-Socialist scholarship has interpreted this saying of Li to mean that in order to lead a nation, one must be humble. Like the masters of the faith, he departed. They must be patient and a humble server who brings those under them to a new stage of enlightenment. Much like he leads the nation, a humble man without desire who enlightens millions on the Way to understanding his divination of the perfect system. True understanding of Technocratic Socialism can only be derived from scholarship; brief readings or vague understandings will multiply falsehood. Falsehood leads to doubts and doubts to dissidence. What is dissidence from perfection if not a failure of one's moral character? Thus dedication to the teachings of Li is required to truly understand Stuipendia. The Socialist Technate is an indivisible entity beyond the nation-state. It is an idea, a dream perhaps. A dream of the perfect world, and under one man, it is realised.
